title: RBAC v2: break-glass elevated session (time-bounded) + explicit audit events
author: Kaitlyn Nguyen
description: Context: As part of RBAC v2, we need a consistent, auditable “break-glass” path for incident-time and support workflows that require temporarily elevated permissions without permanently changing role assignments. This PR adds the plumbing for time-bounded elevated sessions, admin-only controls around granting/revoking, and explicit audit events for each lifecycle transition. Changes: (1) Control plane API: new admin endpoints to create/revoke/list elevated sessions, backed by a signed session token (opaque to clients) and persisted metadata; (2) Authz evaluation: request context now supports an optional elevated_session_id that is only honored when verified + unexpired + scoped to the org; elevated sessions are evaluated as an additional role set (union) and are never used to bypass hard denies (deny reasons still logged); (3) Console/backend wiring: admin-only “Break-glass sessions” page guarded behind new permissions and hidden behind a feature flag; (4) Audit logging: emits dedicated events for elevated session create/activate/revoke/expire, and enriches downstream authz decision logs with elevated_session_id when present; (5) Safety constraints: default TTL 60m (configurable per env), max TTL 4h, per-org rate limit, and server-side reason required (“incident_id”/“ticket”/freeform) for create; (6) Testing: unit tests for TTL enforcement + signature validation, integration tests covering end-to-end creation -> use -> expiration, and a negative test ensuring non-admins cannot mint sessions. Rollout: gated by feature flag rbac_v2_break_glass_sessions (off by default); staging on for on-call validation; production enablement will be coordinated with ENG-5389 migration stages. Notes: This does not implement support impersonation UI; it only enables the elevated session mechanism + auditability so we can build higher-level workflows safely. Manual QA: created session as Org Admin, confirmed audit events, then hit a protected endpoint and verified allow decision includes elevated_session_id; waited for TTL in test mode and confirmed deny + expire event. Screenshots/log snippets included in comments.
commits: audit: emit elevated_session.* lifecycle events + enrich authz decision logs
tests: integration coverage for session TTL + revocation
docs: internal README for on-call validation + local testing
illustrative_snippets: New permission gates (policy bundle work is in a separate PR): rbacv2:permissions: - support.break_glass.session.create - support.break_glass.session.revoke - support.break_glass.session.read

Audit event shape (excerpt): { "event_type": "elevated_session.created", "actor_id": "usr_...", "org_id": "org_...", "target_user_id": "usr_...", "ttl_seconds": 3600, "reason": "INC-2217: production latency incident", "elevated_session_id": "es_...", "policy_version": "v0.1" }
Evaluator behavior (excerpt): effective_roles = base_roles UNION elevated_session.roles; if elevated_session.invalid -> ignore + log decision_reason=ELEVATED_SESSION_INVALID
review_conversation: Marcus Lin: We need to be crystal clear that this isn’t a bypass. Can we ensure deny-overrides still applies even with elevated roles? Also require a reason string and enforce a max TTL server-side.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Yep. Updated evaluator so elevated roles are additive only; deny reason codes still emitted. Added required reason + MAX_TTL_SECONDS constant (4h) enforced in API and store layer.

Kevin Osei: For auditability, I’d like explicit lifecycle events rather than relying on authz decision logs. Specifically: created, revoked, expired, and “used/activated”. Also include elevated_session_id in normal authz logs when present.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Added elevated_session.created/revoked/expired and elevated_session.activated (emitted once per session per user, idempotent via a marker). Also added elevated_session_id to authz decision log fields.
Sean Gallagher: Operationally, we need a per-org throttle so on-call doesn’t accidentally create dozens of sessions. Also make sure there’s an easy way to revoke all sessions during an incident.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Added rate limit (5 creates / 10 min / org) and a bulk revoke endpoint (admin-only) plus an internal-only CLI command for SRE to revoke all for an org.
Rafael Mendes: Please ensure the elevated session cannot be created by Support unless they already have the new permissions. We should also log the target user explicitly (who is being elevated).
Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Confirmed: endpoints are guarded by support.break_glass.session.* permissions and only exposed under /admin; added target_user_id to all lifecycle events.
Allison Grant: Logging fields should be stable and match the exporter schema. Please add decision_reason enums for invalid/expired/revoked session cases (so dashboards can group).
Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Added decision_reason codes: ELEVATED_SESSION_EXPIRED / _REVOKED / _INVALID_SIGNATURE / _ORG_MISMATCH. Also added integration test asserting these codes appear.
Marcus Lin: Looks good after changes. Approving, but please keep the feature flag off by default and coordinate production enablement with the migration playbook.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Acknowledged; default is off in config, and enablement will be tracked under ENG-5389.
merge_outcome: Merged (squash) into main; feature flag remains disabled by default; follow-up work tracked in ENG-5389 for staged rollout and in policy bundle PR for role mapping.
